Everything below is in `SiftOrder/src/main/java/com/siftit/` (`domain/emailReceiving/` and `jobs/`). I read the main handler and grepped the rest; I didn't read `EmailParser.java`, `FallbackMimeParser.java` or `InvoiceRecipientResolver.java` in full. Their causes are inferred from the grep hits.

Processing runs in `ParseInvoiceEmailsJob.runParseInvoiceJob` (`jobs/ParseInvoiceEmailsJob.java:21`). It calls `InvoiceEmailService.handleUnparsedEmails`, which scans the S3 `invoices/` prefix.

| # | Reason | Where it's recorded |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Not running in a non-dev environment. In dev, `handleUnparsedEmails` returns immediately (`InvoiceEmailService.java:91`). | Nowhere. The email stays in S3 `invoices/`. |
| 2 | The email can't be parsed as MIME. `FallbackMimeParser` throws `UnparsableMessageException` after two attempts (`FallbackMimeParser.java:40,50`). | Logged by `orderlyLogger.logException` (`InvoiceEmailService.java:182`). The file moves to S3 `unparsable/<key>` (`:183`). No `EmailReceivingRecord` is written. |
| 3 | Any other exception in `handleEmail`, such as S3, DB or parser failure (`EmailParser.java:51`, `EmailAttachmentExtractor.java:202`). | Logged with `failedEmailFile` metadata (`InvoiceEmailService.java:168`) and again at `:185`. The file stays in `invoices/` and is retried on the next run. No DB record. |
| 4 | No recipient address looks like `<id>@invoices…`. | `errors` gets "We could not find an email that looked like it was addressed to us…" (`:163`). The S3 key becomes `noLocalPart/…` (`:162`). |
| 5 | The recipient's local part isn't a known restaurant ID, or isn't numeric. The lookup swallows exceptions (`:200-202`). | `errors` gets "`<x>` was not a known rest id…" (`:160`). The S3 key becomes `unknown/<localPart>/…` (`:159`). |
| 6 | Recipient resolution failed on the to, cc or bcc headers. | `errors` gets "Exception trying to add to, cc, or bcc emails" (`InvoiceRecipientResolver.java:76`). |
| 7 | The restaurant exists but is inactive. | `errors` gets "Restaurant was not marked active" (`:125`). The attachment is skipped. |
| 8 | The attachment is the wrong type. Only JPEG, PNG, BMP, PDF, JPG and GIF count as images (`:52`), and TXT or CSV are handled separately (`:53`). A PDF with no extension or an odd one is rejected. | `errors` gets "`<name>` was not image or text type file" (`:141`). |
| 9 | The attachment is TXT or CSV and the sender's domain has no supplier mapping. Only `rnc.sysco.com` is mapped (`:69`). | `errors` gets "`<name>` did not have a supplier mapping" (`:138`). |
| 10 | Saving the attachment or grouping threw an exception (`saveNewGroupingForInvoice` or `addInvoiceAttachment`, `:129-130`). | `errors` gets "`<name>` -- `<message>`" (`:144`). |
| 11 | The PDF is inline, embedded or too large, so it isn't extracted as an attachment. There's a test fixture for this: `email_with_large_logo_no_invoice_attachment.eml`. | Nothing explicit. The name is missing from `allAttachments`, or the file shows up in `allAttachments` but not in `attachmentsMoved`. |

For causes 4 to 10, the `errors`, `allAttachments` and `attachmentsMoved` fields are saved in an `EmailReceivingRecord` (`InvoiceEmailService.java:166`, table `emailReceivingRecord`, `EmailReceivingRecord.java:15-30`). You can read them through `getErrors(start, end)` (`InvoiceEmailService.java:243`), which the admin `AdminEmailReceivingWebService` and the AdminUi `invoiceEmails` page use. Causes 2 and 3 only appear in the application logs under the `InvoiceEmail` tag.
